local_articles.title: Back-to-back sprint wins for Tim Merlier in Tour de France, Tadej Pogacar keeps overall lead
local_articles.snippet: BERGERAC, France - Belgian Tim Merlier claimed his second straight Tour de France sprint stage win on July 11, as the Soudal Quick-Step rider pulled off another last-second attack in stage eight of the race. Merlier, who won stage seven with a similar late surge on July 10, waited till the last 400 metres to make his move. His raw power was enough to carry him past Jasper Philipsen, Biniam Girmay and others who had positioned themselves for the sprint finish. Four-time champion Tadej Pogacar (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) retained his overall lead after the flat 180.4km ride from Perigueux to Bergerac, while Jonas Vingegaard (Visma-Lease a Bike) stayed second in the race for the yellow jersey, 2 minutes and 42 seconds off the lead. “Just before the last corner I was a bit boxed in, then I almost crashed - I thought it was over... local_articles.title: Heatwave forces Tour de France organisers to shorten stage nine
local_articles.snippet: BERGERAC, France - Stage nine of the Tour de France on July 12 will be shortened by 30km due to heat risks, race organisers said on July 11, though it will retain its originally planned start and finish points. The stage from Malemort to Ussel, which was originally scheduled for 185.5km, will now follow a 155.5km route, the organisers said in a statement. “Meteo-France has placed the department of Correze on red alert due to an exceptionally intense heatwave,” the statement said. “In light of this... the race will divert from the original route in the neutral zone, taking the D921 and heading from Brive-la-Gaillarde straight to Lanteuil, 147.8km from the finish in Ussel.” Western Europe experienced its warmest June on record, leading to a surge in heat-related deaths. local_articles.title: Road captains, the Tour de France’s cool, calm customers
local_articles.snippet: BORDEAUX – While Tour de France contenders battle to gain time on their rivals, sprinters seek stage wins and breakaway specialists sniff out opportunities, road captains are keeping an eye on everyone. Every team has one but their role is not always obvious, either for fans watching along the side of the road, or for those glued to their television sets. The road captains, the riders who exude “calmness” and “selflessness”, are the ones who organise their team-mates, protect their team leaders and act as the squad’s brains on the road. One of the most experienced road captains at the Tour is Australian Luke Durbridge of Jayco-AlUla. “I think experience, knowledge, just selflessness. He’s just in there for the team,” said his sporting director Mathew Hayman, a former Paris-Roubaix winner. On July 9 (Reuters), the PHLX chip index surged another +3.06% (second straight rally, IT +1.65%, Nasdaq +1.30%), likely lifting Nvidia near ~$5.0T (~$350B-$430B / ~7.5%-9.3% ahead of Apple at ~$4.60T and ~13%-14% ahead of Alphabet at ~$4.41T). OpenAI has become one of the world's most valuable private companies. China's tech firms are judged less by valuation than by their ability to build fast, cut costs and capture global market share. Beijing treats tech less as a financial asset than as industrial infrastructure, which explains why China is simultaneously competitive in batteries, EVs, drones, solar panels, high-speed rail, robotics and increasingly AI. Intense domestic competition, often marked by brutal price wars, compresses profits but produces firms exceptionally well prepared for global competition. questions.title: Which driver will rank second in the Formula One drivers' championship immediately after the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix?
questions.background: The drivers' championship standings reflect cumulative points earned during the season, with ties resolved under Formula One's championship rules.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The post-race drivers' championship standings published by the FIA or Formula One. Resolution : Resolve to the driver ranked second in the championship standings following the Belgian Grand Prix scheduled for July 19, 2026, before any subsequent race takes place. Accepted Answer Format : The driver's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Post-Silverstone British GP (July 5, Reuters/FIA) turns the post-Spa P2 standings race into a pure two-driver contest with a significant structural advantage for George Russell. Charles Leclerc won behind the safety car while Russell stayed out to finish P2 (+18) ahead of Lewis Hamilton in P3 (+15, stewards took no further action on his yellow-flag investigation after Ferrari's late pitstop dropped him behind Russell), and Kimi Antonelli scored 0 (P16 after a front-left wheel shield kerb failure and 5s track limits penalty). With only ONE non-sprint race left before resolution (Belgian GP, July 19, max 25 pts, no fastest-lap point), standings are: Antonelli 179 (5 wins), Russell 154 (2 wins), Hamilton 147 (1 win), Leclerc 108 (1 win). Antonelli is mathematically guaranteed P1 (even a Russell win + Antonelli 0 ties at 179, which Antonelli wins 5-3 on win countback), and Leclerc (max 133) is mathematically eliminated—removing Antonelli's 0.005 tail completely. Russell expanded his lead over Hamilton from +4 to +7 pts AND holds the win-countback tiebreak (2 vs 1), meaning Hamilton must outscore Russell by >=8 pts at Spa (or win Spa while Russell finishes P2 and win P2-finish countback, where Russell already holds multiple P2s including Spain and Silverstone). Monte Carlo Spa simulations blending Mercedes's power-circuit edge (9/9 poles in 2026) with Ferrari's strong high-speed Silverstone form (2 wins in last 3 races) and ~9-10% DNF/rain chaos place Russell at 68-73% (baseline 0.70, up from 0.63) and Hamilton at 0.30 (down from 0.365).

questions.current_reasoning: Rogers remains at the World Cup with England (quarterfinal vs Norway on July 11; Straits Times July 10) with no completed transfer yet. Conditional on Rogers leaving Villa, capping unconfirmed-bid Arsenal strictly at 0.65 (0.67 -> 0.65), nudging Chelsea (0.14 -> 0.15) and Man City (0.05 -> 0.06), and replacing PSG (0.03) with Liverpool (0.05) leaves 5% residual for PSG/Real Madrid/Bayern/other.
